q: Which company introduced the 7-inch single at 45 rpm in January 1949?
options: Columbia
Decca
RCA Victor
Capitol
why: RCA Victor launched its 45 the day after Columbia announced a 33 1/3 single. The LP ended up as the album and the 45 as the single.

q: What is a lacquer, in record making?
options: An aluminum disc coated in lacquer that the groove is first cut into
The clear coat sprayed on a finished record
The varnish that seals the paper label
A plastic sleeve that protects the stampers
why: The lacquer is an aluminum plate with a thick lacquer coat, cut in real time on a lathe, one per side. Everything pressed later is copied from it.

q: Why do cutting engineers usually keep the bass in mono?
options: Mono bass sounds louder on small speakers
Stereo bass differences make big vertical groove swings that can mistrack or lift the cutter
Plants charge extra for stereo bass
The RIAA curve removes stereo below 500 Hz
why: The side (difference) signal moves the groove up and down. Large low-frequency differences between channels can narrow the groove until a stylus cannot track it, or lift the cutter head off the lacquer.

The machine that trims the flash
A metal negative of the groove, mounted in the press to mold the record
The engineer who signs the dead wax
why: Stampers are plated from a mother, chrome plated and mounted in the press. Because they are negatives, they press grooves into the vinyl.

q: What does a 180 gram LP share with a standard-weight LP of about 140 grams?
options: The same stampers and groove depth
A deeper groove
A longer playing time per side
A different cutting curve
why: Disc Makers says 180 gram records use the same stampers and groove depth as standard weight. The weight is printed on the sticker; the quality of the cut is not.

q: Why do some 12-inch records spin at 45 rpm instead of 33 1/3?
options: To fit more songs on a side
Because 45 rpm records need no RIAA curve
Because DJ mixers only accept 45 rpm
The groove passes the stylus faster, leaving more room for short high-frequency wavelengths
why: At the outer edge a 12-inch moves about 28.3 inches per second at 45, against almost 21 at 33 1/3. The cost is time: a 45 side holds far less music.

q: On a UK Decca record, the stamper code uses the word BUCKINGHAM. What does "NN" mean?
options: The 11th stamper
The 66th stamper
The 14th stamper
A new number after a recut
why: In BUCKINGHAM each letter is a digit: B=1 through M=0, with N=6. So NN is the 66th stamper.

q: A former Columbia cutting engineer explained the lacquer sets 1A to 1F. What did they mean?
options: 1A was the first cut and 1F the sixth
1A to 1F were test pressings
All six were first cuttings, sent two each to three plants
Each letter marked a different mastering engineer
why: Phil Brown said 1A and 1B went to Pitman, 1C and 1D to Terre Haute, 1E and 1F to Santa Maria. The belief that A came before B and C is wrong.

q: What does a phono preamp do?
options: Adds gain and applies the inverse RIAA curve
Converts the signal to digital
Removes surface noise
Sets the tracking force
why: A cartridge's signal is far below line level. The phono stage boosts it and undoes the cutting EQ, restoring bass and taming treble.

q: What usually happens if the tracking force is set too light?
options: The record plays faster
The stylus wears out sooner
The bass gets louder
The stylus can lose the groove and skip
why: Tracking force should match the cartridge maker's figure. Too light and the record skips, too heavy and it can damage the groove.

q: What feature made the Technics SL-1200 suit DJs?
options: A built-in mixer
Direct drive, with high torque, a near-instant start and steady speed
A belt that could be swapped quickly
An automatic tonearm return
why: With the platter on the motor, the deck could be pushed around or spun backward without harm. Scratching would destroy a belt drive.

q: What is on a timecode record used with a digital vinyl system?
options: A compressed copy of the DJ's music
Silence, so the needle does not wear
A control signal that software reads for speed, direction and position
A backup of the mixer's settings
why: The software reads the control signal from the turntable for speed, direction and position, and plays a digital file to match.

q: On the Goldmine scale, which grade has surface noise that is evident, especially in soft passages, but does not overpower the music?
options: Near Mint
Very Good Plus
Good
Very Good
why: That is the Goldmine definition of VG. VG+ shows only slight signs of wear, while Good plays through with significant noise.

q: In one label's published breakdown of a $24 LP sold in an independent shop, roughly how much did the artist get?
why: Colemine Records' figures gave the retailer $8.49, the manufacturer $6.03, the distributor $3.10, and the label and artist about $3.19 each - numbers the label says apply to that one release.

q: What is BioVinyl, launched by optimal media in 2023?
options: A record made from sugars and starches
Still PVC, made with feedstock from used cooking oil or industrial waste gases instead of petroleum
An injection-molded PET record
Recycled records with the labels punched out
why: BioVinyl is bio-attributed PVC: the same plastic, with the petroleum feedstock swapped for used cooking oil or waste gases. The lower CO2 footprint is the maker's own claim, with no number attached.

q: Where is GZ Media, described as the world's largest record presser?
options: Germany, near Hamburg
The US, in Nashville
Japan, in Yokohama
Czechia, in a village near Prague
why: GZ Media in Lodenice pressed more than 55 million records in 2021. It also runs plants in North America and France.
